subject: KYCStream - identity-audit trace retention exception request
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria@kycstream.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@kycstream.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Retention exception request for identity-audit traces

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week — KYCStream is hopeful Redwood can meet a narrow retention requirement tied to our audit obligations. Our compliance team reviewed the platform: most logs meet the 30-day default, but the identity-audit traces (redacted session keys + action-level events) need to be retained for 180 days for our regulator in LATAM.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 
- Provide a documented exception pathway to retain the identity-audit traces for 180 days for a named tenant?
- Produce evidence that these traces can be isolated and exported on request (CAIQ / SIG artifacts preferred)?
- Commit to a proof-of-delete workflow and provide an example artifact we can include in our audit pack?

Attached is our requirements doc (kyc_requirements_2026.pdf). We are not asking for a general policy change — just a tenant-specific carveout with compensating controls (pseudonymization + encrypted escrow).

Legal is cc'd; they may send redlines to the contract amendment if we can align on technical feasibility. Ideally we’d have a feasibility confirmation by EOD Monday so we can scope procurement.

Thanks,

Maria Lopez
Head of Compliance
KYCStream
attachments: kyc_requirements_2026.pdf
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.example.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria@kycstream.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.example.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retention exception request for identity-audit traces

Maria —

Appreciate the clear ask and the doc. Short answer: we have patterns to support tenant-scoped retention exceptions, but this one has operational and evidence-delivery implications we need Security and Product to sign off on. I’ve looped in Neha (Security) and Kim (Product pricing/contracts).

High-level plan:
1) Security feasibility check (Neha) — confirm whether pseudonymization + encrypted escrow is sufficient and what evidence we can produce (SOC2 artifact mapping + CAIQ sections).
2) Implementation estimate (Product/Eng) — engineering changes, retention config, and export path.
3) Contract amendment draft (Kim) — narrow SLA/compensating controls and remediation SLAs.

Maria — can you confirm a couple of things to help scoping:
- Which exact object types are in scope (session traces vs. full request logs)?
- Do you require raw logs or a redacted audit bundle for audit reviewers?
- Any preferred custody model for the escrow (S3 with KMS key held by customer vs Redwood-managed HSM)?

If legal provides redlines we’ll review in parallel. We should be able to get a technical feasibility note Monday afternoon PST.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference, Inc.
From: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.example.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.example.com>, Maria Lopez <maria@kycstream.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retention exception request for identity-audit traces

Hi all,

Thanks — tagging on the technical and compliance details from Security. We reviewed the kyc_requirements_2026.pdf and ran a quick internal test on a tenant mirror. Summary:

- Feasibility: We can support a tenant-scoped 180-day retention for a limited set of identity-audit trace objects (configured via tenant policy). Those objects are stored separately from general debug traces and can be configured to be pseudonymized at ingest (SHA-256 keyed salt) and encrypted at rest with a customer-managed KMS key.

- Evidence we can provide:
  * SOC 2 mapping: we can produce an artifact that shows control points (CC6.3, CC7.1) with screenshots of retention config and the CI pipeline that enforces retention TTLs.
  * CAIQ / SIG: we can export a CAIQ supplement that documents the exception and the compensating controls (pseudonymization, access controls, export procedure).
  * Proof-of-delete: we can provide a sample signed manifest showing delete transactions (hashes + timestamps) and the workflow used to trigger deletion.

- Escrow options: two paths supported
  1) Redwood-managed encrypted escrow (we hold the encrypted artifacts and certify deletion on request).
  2) Customer-managed key in their cloud KMS with an export-to-S3 escrow bucket (customer retains key control).

- Operational constraints:
  * We need a formal Exception Request Form signed by customer legal (DocuSign link below) that scopes objects and period.
  * Implementation ETA: small config + policy + evidence pack — ~7 business days after Exception Request acceptance. Larger work (if additional export tooling required) may push to ~3 weeks.

I uploaded a short draft of the CAIQ supplement and a sample proof-of-delete manifest to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleEvidence. Also added the DocuSign Exception Form draft: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/DOC-2026-DY34712.

Next steps: Maria, if Legal can sign the Exception Request Form we can begin a scoped implementation and deliver the evidence_manifest.zip upon completion. We will include the CAIQ supplement and a SOC2-control mapping document in the evidence bundle.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Maria, Legal —

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Neha — that is exactly the level of detail we needed. Per Neha’s note and Kim’s review, here are the agreed next steps and timeline we will commit to if KYCStream signs the Exception Request Form:

1) Exception acceptance: KYCStream Legal signs the DocuSign Exception Request (link above).
2) Tech implementation: Redwood Security/Engineering enables tenant policy (180d TTL) and configures pseudonymization + KMS encryption. ETA: 7 business days.
3) Evidence delivery: upon completion Redwood will deliver: CAIQ-supplement.pdf, SOC2-control-mapping.pdf, evidence_manifest.zip (signed proof-of-delete example).
4) Contract amendment: Kim will circulate a narrow amendment that defines the scope, retention period, escrow custody choice, and remediation SLAs.

Kim, will you send the amendment draft (redlines_contract_amendment.docx) to Legal and Maria now? I’ll mark the matter high priority on our implementation queue once DocuSign is signed.

Maria — please confirm the custody model you prefer (Redwood-managed encrypted escrow vs customer KMS). If you want customer KMS we’ll attach key rotation requirements to the amendment.

Appreciate the partnership — we aim to make this auditable and minimally invasive to your workflow.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
